When a map value is being freed
column2: we loop over all of the fields of the

column1: corresponding BPF object and issue the appropriate cleanup calls
corresponding to the field's type. If the field is a referenced kptr
atomically xchg the value out of the map
destructor on whatever was there before (or bpf_obj_drop() it if it was
a local kptr).
Currently
column2: we always invoke the destructor (either bpf_obj_drop() or the

column1: kptr's registered destructor) on any KPTR_REF-type field in a map
if there wasn't a value in the map. This means that any function serving
as the kptr's KF_RELEASE destructor must always treat the argument as
possibly NULL
column2: as the following can and regularly does happen:

column1: void *xchgd_field;
/* No value was in the map
xchgd_field = (void *)xchg(unsigned long *field_ptr
field->kptr.dtor(xchgd_field);
These are odd semantics to impose on KF_RELEASE kfuncs -- BPF programs
are prohibited by the verifier from passing NULL pointers to KF_RELEASE
kfuncs
column2: so it doesn't make sense to require this of BPF programs

column1: not the main kernel destructor path. It's also unnecessary to invoke any
cleanup logic for local kptrs. If there is no object there
nothing to drop.
So as to allow KF_RELEASE kfuncs to fully assume that an argument is
non-NULL
column2: this patch updates a KPTR_REF's destructor to only be invoked

column1: when a non-NULL value is xchg'd out of the kptr map field.
